questions.q: Which chapter closed Lesson 1's "no visibility into dependencies" gap?
options: Chapter 2 — Snowflake Foundations
Chapter 4 — generated docs and the lineage graph
Chapter 5 — Python Ingestion Layer
Chapter 7 — the Power BI layer
questions.explain: dbt docs generate and the lineage graph, built in Chapter 4, are what made dependencies visible to anyone, not just developers.

questions.q: What did this Advanced tier deliberately assume already existed, rather than rebuilding from scratch?
options: A finished Power BI report
The Beginner and Intermediate tiers' stg_jaffle_shop__* staging models and early marts
A fully configured GitHub Actions workflow
A completed Python ingestion script
questions.explain: Lesson 1 named this assumption directly — this tier spends its time on governance, testing, ingestion, and CI/CD, not re-teaching ref() and staging from zero.

questions.q: What "deploy job" does this lesson suggest as a realistic next step beyond this capstone's CI pipeline?
options: A job that deletes the RAW schema automatically every night
A second CI/CD job, separate from the pull-request check, that runs dbt build --target prod automatically on merge to main
A job that disables all RBAC roles for easier access
A job that replaces Power BI with a different BI tool
questions.explain: A deploy job that builds prod on merge — the same two-job split this path's Git/CI-CD course covers — is a natural extension beyond just testing pull requests.

questions.q: How many custom generic tests does this platform have as built in this capstone, and what does the lesson say a real team typically accumulates?
options: Zero built here; a real team adds its first one later
One (non_negative); a real team accumulates dozens, each tied to a specific business rule that's caused a real problem before
Ten, one per model in the project
This capstone intentionally avoids custom tests entirely
questions.explain: The capstone built exactly one custom generic test as a teaching example; real platforms grow a much larger library of them over time.

questions.q: What does this lesson suggest as a realistic eventual replacement for cron or Task Scheduler running the Python ingestion script?
options: Removing the ingestion script entirely once dbt is governed
dbt Cloud's own scheduler or an orchestrator like Airflow, once enough scheduled jobs accumulate to need centralized monitoring
Running the script manually every morning instead
Moving the script's logic directly into a Snowflake stored procedure with no scheduler at all
questions.explain: As scheduled jobs multiply, centralizing them in a real orchestrator or dbt Cloud's scheduler becomes the realistic next step over ad hoc cron entries.
